scheme_name: Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Marriage Incentives & Support
description:
The Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Marriage Incentives & Support scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2008. 

This scheme aims to provide social and economic rehabilitation to individuals who have been cured of leprosy. 

Leprosy, also known as Hansen's disease, has historically led to significant social stigma and discrimination against affected individuals. 

The Government of India recognized the need to support cured leprosy patients in reintegrating into society. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to encourage marriage among cured leprosy persons. 

The scheme also aims to provide financial assistance and support to these individuals to help them lead a dignified life. 

The scheme specifically targets cured leprosy patients who are of marriageable age. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is aimed at alleviating the economic burden associated with marriage. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive a one-time marriage incentive of ₹1 lakh. 

This amount is provided to help cover the costs associated with marriage ceremonies and related expenses. 

The scheme also aims to reduce the stigma associated with leprosy by promoting social acceptance. 

The initiative is part of a broader effort to ensure that cured leprosy patients can live with dignity and respect. 

To be eligible for the marriage incentive, individuals must be cured of leprosy. 

They must also be between the ages of 18 and 45 years. 

The income criteria for eligibility stipulate that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed ₹1 lakh. 

This income limit is set to ensure that the benefits reach the economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and designed to be accessible. 

Interested individuals must submit an application form to the designated authority in their district. 

The application form can be obtained from the local health department or the district leprosy rehabilitation office. 

Along with the application form, applicants must provide specific documents. 

These documents include a certificate of cure from a registered medical practitioner. 

Applicants must also submit proof of age, such as a birth certificate or school leaving certificate. 

Additionally, an income certificate is required to verify that the applicant meets the income criteria. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local authorities. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If the application is approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account. 

The disbursement of funds is usually completed within 15 days of approval. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 

The National Leprosy Eradication Programme is responsible for overseeing the execution of this scheme. 

State health departments also play a crucial role in implementing the scheme at the local level. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework aimed at the rehabilitation of persons affected by leprosy. 

It is designed to empower cured leprosy patients and promote their social inclusion. 

The Government of India has allocated a budget of ₹10 crore for this scheme in the financial year 2022-2023. 

This budget is intended to support the marriage incentives and additional rehabilitation measures. 

The scheme has successfully facilitated the marriage of numerous cured leprosy patients since its inception. 

It has contributed to reducing the stigma associated with leprosy in various communities. 

Awareness campaigns are also conducted to educate the public about leprosy and the importance of social acceptance. 

These campaigns aim to dispel myths and misconceptions surrounding the disease. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have successfully married with the help of the financial assistance. 

Many beneficiaries have reported improved social standing and acceptance in their communities. 

The Government of India continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme's effectiveness. 

Regular assessments are conducted to ensure that the objectives are being met. 

The scheme is part of a comprehensive approach to tackle the challenges faced by cured leprosy patients. 

It aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to health and well-being. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of mental health and social support for cured leprosy patients. 

The initiative reflects the government's commitment to promoting equality and social justice. 

By providing financial assistance for marriage, the scheme aims to empower individuals and promote family stability. 

The scheme has also inspired similar initiatives in various states across India. 

Local governments have started to implement their own programs to support cured leprosy patients. 

These initiatives often include vocational training and employment opportunities. 

The success of the Marriage Incentives & Support scheme has encouraged further investment in leprosy rehabilitation programs. 

The government aims to create a more inclusive society where cured leprosy patients can thrive. 

Overall, the Rehabilitation of Cured Leprosy Persons: Marriage Incentives & Support scheme represents a significant step towards social integration and empowerment. 

It provides a much-needed lifeline to individuals who have faced significant challenges due to their past health conditions. 

The scheme not only addresses financial needs but also promotes social acceptance and dignity. 

The ongoing commitment of the government to this cause is crucial for the continued success of the initiative. 

As of October 2023, the scheme remains an essential part of India's efforts to support cured leprosy patients. 

It highlights the importance of comprehensive rehabilitation and social support systems. 

The government encourages eligible individuals to take advantage of this scheme for their benefit. 

For more information, individuals can contact their local health department or visit the official website of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 

This scheme exemplifies the government's dedication to improving the lives of marginalized communities in India.
